card.name: Held objects in descriptions of figures
card.fires_on: Words like a, and, carrying, wearing or holding that come right before an object held or worn, in descriptions of a figure's attributes. Seen mostly in descriptions of the Muses and in coat-of-arms symbols.

modes.label: Article before held item
modes.description: The word a after holding, wearing or carrying, just before the object is named.
modes.example: She is often depicted holding<< a>> comedy mask and wearing an ivy gar

modes.label: Carrying/wearing verbs
modes.description: The verb itself, in 'depicted wearing' or 'and carrying', just before the attribute.
modes.example: Cleio is often depicted wearing a laurel garland and<< carrying>> parchments.

modes.label: Joined emblems
modes.description: The word and linking paired emblems in a coat-of-arms description.
modes.example: The Communist red star and hammer<< and>> sickle were replaced with the national shrine

card.writes: It pushes toward words for held objects and implements, such as tools, crate and scales.
card.plain: It fires where a text is about to say what object a figure holds, carries or wears.
